node-1.label: Development of an epiretinal membrane in the right eye

node-2.label: Woman in her 70s with pseudophakia and history of chronic noninfectious bilateral uveitis and recurrent cystoid macular edema was being treated with serial injections of 0.7-mg dexamethasone intravitreal implants

node-3.label: Best-corrected visual acuity was approximately 20/50 OD and 20/200 OS

node-4.label: One week after the initial procedure: visual acuity was 20/100 OD, intraocular pressure was 10 mm Hg, there was 40% to 50% gas fill, and the retina was attached

why.why: Radiologist and laboratory analyses both interpret the dexamethasone implant adherent to the retina five days after vitrectomy, with retinal indentation/compression and linear hyperautofluorescence in the superior macula, as strong support for an inflammatory mechanism. This is integrated with the patient's chronic bilateral uveitis, recurrent cystoid macular edema, and implant treatment; the laboratory expert states the inflammatory hypothesis is confirmed at this stage. Confidence is therefore raised from 0.55 to 0.70.

Post-surgical ERM remains plausible because of pseudophakia, serial injections, and recent gas tamponade, but both experts explicitly characterize it as less supported than the inflammatory mechanism. The imaging findings of implant adherence and hyperautofluorescence are interpreted primarily as inflammatory/mechanical rather than purely post-surgical. Confidence is reduced from 0.35 to 0.25.

The laboratory analysis states that the inflammatory context outweighs the weaker vitreoretinal explanation, and the radiologist recommends clinical correlation with uveitis activity rather than suggesting an independent vitreoretinal process. No new evidence implicates vitreoretinal disease, so confidence is reduced from 0.08 to 0.05.

Both expert analyses explicitly regard idiopathic ERM as very unlikely given the strong inflammatory and procedural context, reinforced by the specific imaging findings of implant adherence, retinal indentation, and hyperautofluorescence. Confidence is lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.
